existing_terminology:
Speech and language difficulties is the SEN category used in Gibraltar school data
The 2024 review records that specific definitions of each type of need are not available
In statute SEND is defined as Supported Educational Needs and Disabilities, not Special
The paediatric service names specific language impairment among the difficulties it supports
existing_identificationCriteria:
A Special Needs Assessment Panel receives, examines and assesses each child referred
Panel is drawn from education, social services and the Gibraltar Health Authority
Panel need not act unless satisfied the parents have been consulted
Threshold: significantly greater difficulty in learning than most children of the age
Not a learning difficulty solely because the teaching language differs from home
existing_referralPathway:
A Department officer may serve written notice requiring a child be examined
A parent may ask the Director to have the child medically examined
Parental consent is not needed for a child to be referred to the panel
Parent must be given notice of the examination and may attend it
existing_serviceModel:
Statute allows SEND provision outside Gibraltar, in a Government school, the home or hospital
Parents said they feel they have to go to Spain to see private therapists (2024 review)
Family-focused therapy programmes are shaped to the needs of the child by the paediatric service
A 2024 review weighs spreading LSAs through mainstream classes against SEN in separate settings
existing_legalEntitlement:
Education and Training Act obliges the Minister to make SEND education provision
Director, on the panel's recommendation, must ascertain which children require SEND
Department of Education must keep its SEND arrangements under review
Parent may appeal a section 47(1) decision to the SEND Review Panel
existing_funding:
Education provided in Government schools is free for children of compulsory school age
For a placement outside Gibraltar the Department may pay fees in part or in full
existing_workforce:
Paediatric service at the Primary Care Centre is staffed by four therapists
The adult service at St Bernard's Hospital is staffed by one therapist
Therapy is delivered at the Centre, in schools, nurseries and in some cases at home
Two paediatric vacancies arose in the twelve months to April 2023, one on retirement
Government said Brexit made recruiting qualified UK specialists harder (2023 release)
existing_outcomesEvidence: Not established from the sources consulted for this entry — the Department of Education pages on gibraltar.gov.gi answer and publish no pupil statistics, and no Gibraltar statistical publication separating special educational needs was located. This entry already records that the Gibraltar register could not be read; the same is true of any outcome reporting. If you work in this system, this is exactly the field to fill in.

Says speech where the English said language, not a statutory label
existing_identificationCriteria:
The head forms a school inclusion team and a separate team for the individual pupil
The pupil's team is teachers, the parent, psychologist and special educator
Support measures follow the disability assessment made by the national assessment system
The plan is due within 30 days of the pupil starting school
existing_referralPathway:
Supplementary teaching is asked for by the pupil, the parent, or on the teacher's view
The class or subject teacher tells the parent within three days of finding the need
Where the school has no specialist of a profile, support centres supply the member
A pupil may move to a resource-centre school by their own or the parent's choice
existing_serviceModel:
SLTs work across health, education, hearing and speech centres, and private practice
The same four-way split as neighbouring Slovenia (Novšak Brce et al., 2023)

existing_legalEntitlement:
Adaptation stops short of a disproportionate or unnecessary burden on the school
Zakon za osnovnoto obrazovanie art 11: schooling organised to include all children
Infrastructure, individualised support and the curriculum are adapted to the pupil
Pupils with disability must have access to buildings, transport and information
existing_funding:
Every child has a right to free and quality primary education
Pupils with disability and escorts get free accessible transport regardless of distance
Affirmative measures include fee exemption for foreign certificates and free transport
existing_workforce:
Of 110 therapists surveyed across the two countries, 48 practised in North Macedonia
95.8% of therapists surveyed were female (Novšak Brce et al., 2023)
Organised services date from 1950, university training from the mid-1980s
A few years later than Slovenia; students also train at the Slovenian university
existing_outcomesEvidence:

Collected by the State Statistical Office on form УОП from every primary school

existing_terminology:
The statutory term is cerinţe educaţionale speciale (mirror, official register 403s)
It turns on schooling adapted to a disability or learning disorder
Difficulties of learning, communication and interaction are named targets
existing_identificationCriteria:
The logoped identifies and evaluates children's language and communication disorders
How many need help follows an initial or complex evaluation under ministry methodology
The logoped selects the evaluation methods, probes and techniques used
Threshold is disorder of language and communication relative to age and school demands
existing_referralPathway:
Complex examination is run by central and local authorised structures
The methodology is approved by the education ministry
Parents may require that determination happens in their presence
existing_serviceModel:
Mainstream schools MAY organise logopedic services where needed
Inclusive education units may be set up for severe disability
The provision is permissive, not a duty on every school
existing_legalEntitlement:
Education for pupils with special educational needs is free by statute
Delivery may be mainstream, in special institutions, or at home
existing_funding:
Budget funding runs on a standard cost per child with an adjustment coefficient
Compensatory funding exists for children with special educational needs
Fees may be charged for study programmes beyond the standard state-funded package
existing_workforce:
Support teachers work in mainstream schools
Logoped is a listed staff category in special education
existing_outcomesEvidence:
BNS breaks the early-education CES count down by type, with speech its own category
Reported in a 2024 UNICEF gap analysis drawing on National Bureau of Statistics data
Speech deficiency is the largest group in early education at 33.1%, ahead of vision at 27.6%
1,667 children with CES or disability received logopedic help in 2023
The school-level BNS release counts only special-school enrolment, with no split by need

existing_terminology:
The umbrella term is élèves à besoins éducatifs particuliers ou spécifiques
Language impairment is named inside that umbrella, not as a standalone category
A 2018 law created specialised psycho-pedagogical competence centres
existing_identificationCriteria:
The statutory test is inability to reach primary core skills in the regular time span
Grounds listed are mental, character, sensorial or motor characteristics
existing_multilingualProvision:
New standardised tests carry an instruction language adapting to each pupil's language profile
The batteries assess reading, written expression and maths, not spoken language
Given by qualified psychologists, pedagogues and orthophonists in ESEB support teams
They separate difficulties tied to the pupil's language profile from specific disorders
Before these, tests built for German-first children had to be used
existing_referralPathway:
Specialised school teachers detect need and monitor schooling locally
Three tiers since the 2018 reform: local, then regional, then national
Regional support teams make the first diagnosis with the school
National competence centres take over only where local support is insufficient
existing_serviceModel:
One of eight national competence centres is dedicated to language and communication
A separate centre covers dyslexia, dyspraxia and dyscalculia
Centres also serve young people over 18 where education or training needs it
existing_legalEntitlement:
A 2011 law entitles pupils to reasonable arrangements in programmes and assessments
Pupils are under the same compulsory schooling duty, ages 4 to 16
An individual support plan may be set by the school inclusion commission
existing_funding: Placement elsewhere: schooling, lodging, stay and travel costs are borne by the State
existing_workforce:
Entry is a bachelor in orthophonie or an equivalent higher-education qualification
The profession is regulated: practising needs a Ministry of Health authorisation
Posts sit in fundamental and secondary education and in childcare services
existing_outcomesEvidence:
Counted by official decision, not by need, so no type of difficulty is separated
The Ministry of Education, Children and Youth supplies the figures
900 primary-age learners held an official decision in 2022/23, 656 of them boys
The count includes children schooled in special establishments abroad
CNI records are reviewed at the transition points, at ages 12 and 16
